technique.how: Measure systolic BP in both arms with the same correctly sized cuff, patient in the same position, ideally simultaneously or in immediate succession and repeated once. A difference >20 mmHg systolic is the conventional positive threshold; pair the reading with palpation of both radial pulses.
technique.prerequisites: Both arms accessible without fistula, lymphedema or arterial line; automated or manual cuff of correct size.
technique.contraindications: Avoid cuff on an arm with AV fistula, recent lymph node dissection, or PICC.

interpretation.positive_finding: A new >20 mmHg inter-arm systolic difference in a patient with acute truncal pain increases the probability of aortic dissection (pooled LR+ 5.7 for pulse/BP differential; ED case-control OR 2.7), but alone it is a weak discriminator.
interpretation.negative_finding: Equal arm pressures do not exclude dissection; only about 31% of dissections show any pulse or BP differential.
interpretation.pitfalls: Inter-arm differences >10 mmHg are common in the general population from subclavian atherosclerosis, and sequential measurements vary with time and arm position; a BP differential without a pulse deficit has poor diagnostic accuracy (DOR 2.7 vs 28.9 for pulse deficit).
interpretation.changes_what: Positive >20 mmHg difference with suspicious pain: image the aorta; a normal result should not lower suspicion.

estimates.population: Consecutive patients with confirmed thoracic aortic dissection across 21 studies (pooled; pulse deficit or BP differential combined)
estimates.reference_standard: Imaging/surgery/autopsy-confirmed dissection in the primary studies
estimates.quote: 31% have pulse deficits or blood pressure differentials … differentials and neurological deficits increase the likelihood of disease (positive LRs, 5.7 and 6.6-33.0, respectively)

sources.citation: Klompas M. Does this patient have an acute thoracic aortic dissection? JAMA. 2002;287(17):2262-2272.
Um SW, Ohle R, Perry JJ. Bilateral blood pressure differential as a clinical marker for acute aortic dissection in the emergency department. Emerg Med J. 2018;35(9):556-558.
Ohle R, Um J, Anjum O, et al. Clinical Examination for Acute Aortic Dissection: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis. Acad Emerg Med. 2018;25(4):397-412.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not rely on a single sequential measurement, or on measurements in an arm with fistula, PICC, or known subclavian stenosis.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: BP differential together with pulse deficit, abrupt tearing pain, hypotension, or neuro deficit demands immediate aortic imaging.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Measurement variability between sequential readings is substantial; Um 2018 concluded that 'potential variability in measurement limits its clinical usefulness'.

extraction_notes: No source isolating inter-arm systolic BP >20 mmHg with sensitivity/specificity/LR was retrievable from abstracts. Estimate 0 is the Klompas 2002 RCE pooled figure for the combined finding 'pulse deficits or blood pressure differentials' (sens 31%, LR+ 5.7; two abstract fragments joined by ellipsis; CI and specificity not in abstract). Um 2018 (ED matched case-control, 111 AAD cases/111 controls) is the only study isolating systolic BP differential >20 mmHg: univariate OR 2.7 (95% CI 1.39-5.25) and diagnostic OR 2.71, vs pulse deficit DOR 28.9 (Abstract). Odds ratios are not LRs and sens/spec are not in the abstract, so no estimate entered; numbers are given in pitfalls for context. Ohle 2018 meta-analysis abstract does not report BP differential. Status partially_quantified: only a combined-finding, single-direction estimate.
